comment: Every place THIS subpackage's ESLint config deliberately differs from obsidian-dev-utils' shared config, and why.
`workflow-scripts/` is a self-contained package - its own package.json, node_modules, tsconfig and eslint config -
so its `scripts/eslint-config.ts` is a SECOND hand copy of that shared config, separate from the one at the repo
root. Nothing had ever compared it to anything. update-npm-deps.ps1 compares the two configs on every dependency
sweep of this directory and fails on anything not recorded here; sweeping the repo root does not sweep this.
The comparison is DIRECTIONAL: only 'obsidian-dev-utils refined something and this copy never took it' is a
finding. A rule this package enables that obsidian-dev-utils turns off is printed as information and never fails.
A key is the finding's identity exactly as the check prints it: <role>|<rule>|<kind>[|<detail>]. The
correspondence runs BOTH ways - an entry describing a divergence that no longer exists fails the sweep too.
`roles` names the file compared at each end. This package has no `scripts/commit.ts` - committing is the root
package's job - so the script role is its own `scripts/lint.ts` against the same file upstream.

script|plugin:unicorn.why: `eslint-plugin-unicorn` is not installed here. This package is four small workflow scripts and a handful of helpers; it carries the tseslint / stylistic / import-x / perfectionist stack and nothing else. Adding the plugin would be a dependency decision, not a config fix.

script|no-console|level.why: Every module here is a CLI entry point or a helper for one, and their output IS their interface. obsidian-dev-utils leaves the rule on everywhere because nothing in that package prints.

script|obsidian-dev-utils/no-async-callb.why: This package vendors two of obsidian-dev-utils' custom rules into `helpers/eslint-rules/`, and registers exactly those two; its `local/` plugin file's `rules` map IS that subset. The two are the ones its own sources can break.

script|obsidian-dev-utils/no-over-cap-wa.why: Not vendored - same two-rule subset. The rule polices an integration suite's `evalInObsidian` wait budget, and nothing here drives Obsidian.

script|obsidian-dev-utils/require-compon.why: Not vendored - same two-rule subset. Obsidian `Component` subclasses are a plugin-authoring shape; these are release-workflow scripts.
